Fact.description:
Something that happened, kept in the sim. Residents only voice it: code decides who tells
it to whom, and who lies about it.

what.description: What happened, in the third person, as it really did. Each knower's memory of it is in their own words.
what.title: What

where.description: A location's id, such as "maker_space", or a map's, such as "high_street".
where.title: Where

about.description: Who it's about, even if those who know it couldn't name them.
about.title: About

known_by.description: The residents who know it, each listed once.
known_by.title: Known By

found_in.description: The clue the player can find it in instead of being told, such as Aris's notes: the interactable's id. Null if only residents can tell it.
found_in.title: Found In

leads.description: Where learning it points the player next, never back to itself.
leads.title: Leads

Fact.title: Fact

HowKnown.description:
How a resident knows a fact: they `did` it, `witnessed` it (saw or heard it happen), or
were `told` it by someone.
HowKnown.title: HowKnown

Incident.description:
The night Aris was attacked, made once at world creation: who attacked her, why, and the
facts around it.

victim.description: Aris, who has been missing since.
victim.title: Victim

attackers.description: The residents who attacked her, one to three.
attackers.title: Attackers

motive.description: Why they did it, written once at world creation and never rewritten.
motive.title: Motive

night.description: When they attacked her, in sim time.
night.title: Night

facts.description: Who did it, why, who saw what and who knows what. Each has its own id, and their leads go to one another.
facts.title: Facts

Incident.title: Incident

JournalEntry.description: Something the player learned about the incident: a fact, or a lie told about one.

fact_id.description: The fact it's about. Several entries can be about one fact.
fact_id.title: Fact Id

text.description: What they learned, as the journal puts it. A lie is written as it was told.
text.title: Text

source.description: Who told them, or the clue they found it in.

flushed.description: Whether the infrared eye saw the resident flush as they told it, which it shows exactly on a lie. Null if the player had no infrared eye then, and for a clue.
flushed.title: Flushed

leads.description: The leads it opened that are still open. Each stays until the player learns its fact, from anyone.
leads.title: Leads

JournalEntry.title: JournalEntry

Knower.description: A resident who knows a fact, how they know it, and how willing they are to tell it.

tells_from.description: The least trust they need in whoever asks before they tell it: 0 tells anyone. Null if they never tell it.
tells_from.title: Tells From

cover.description: What they say instead of telling it, when they lie, e.g. "I was home all night." Code decides when they lie, as for other lies, so the infrared eye reads it exactly. Null if they keep quiet rather than lie.
cover.title: Cover

Knower.title: Knower

Lead.description: Where the trail goes next: someone to ask or somewhere to look, which turns up a fact.

fact_id.description: The fact following it turns up.
fact_id.title: Fact Id

text.description: For the journal, e.g. "Kofi paints in the lane at night. Ask him what he saw."
text.title: Text

Lead.title: Lead

Source.description: Who told the player something, or the clue they found it in.

id.description: The resident's id, or the clue's interactable's.
id.title: Id

name.description: As the journal names them, e.g. "Kofi" or "Aris's notes".
name.title: Name

Source.title: Source

SourceKind.description:
Where the player learned something: a `resident` told them, or they found a `clue`, such
as Aris's notes or a terminal.
SourceKind.title: SourceKind

description:
The incident and the player's journal of it, saved with the world. One object holds both,
so it can be restored in place before the world has made an incident.

incident.description: Null until the world makes it, as in a save from before it.

journal.description: What the player has learned, in the order they learned it.
journal.title: Journal

title: Investigation
